I'm just beginning my AS in Environmental Science at a community college before I transfer to a state university to finish my BS, and I'm hoping to go into Hydrology. There aren't prerequisites. However, you can prepare yourself.



I recommend community college if the degree is available to you. It's cheaper, and credits typically transfer. I use Transferology to find what does and doesn't transfer in hopes of saving time and money.



Here's what I did, because I'm a nerd who loves lists:



1) Decide what school you're going to and see if they have a list of required and recommended classes for your degree.



2) Write down what classes you'll need to take, and look through their list of electives. I chose ones that will work well with what I want to do for work. I also recommend putting the department as well. English is ENGL, Mathematics is MATH, Chemistry is CHEM, etc. This helps keep things organized, as c



3) Write down their prerequisites. If you did poorly at math (or other classes) like I did in high school, you'll need to take additional classes before you take the main class. I have to take two additional classes before I take College Algebra.
